title: Fork margin against the effect of 40 random pushes
caption: Each point is one of iteration 4's 40 random directions at alpha 2 in Qwen3-8B bf16. (a) Connected components: the teacher-forced fork margin at generated tokens 10-11 against the correct share off the default (Spearman 0.80, 95% interval 0.62 to 0.91; a placebo that shuffles which fork tokens lead to which algorithm reaches 0.80 in 18% of 200 permutations, so the margin acts through the probability that stays on the default fork tokens). (b) Shortest path, which has no single fork: the committed fallback, the 48-token opening log likelihood ratio, against the same share (Spearman 0.15, p 0.18). The fork claim holds where a fork exists and fails where the decision falls late.
summary: The fork margin predicts which random pushes change the algorithm on connected components, and the opening LLR fails on shortest path where no early fork exists.
